Nothing in the repo can run `uv run troupe config …` yet, so testing `main` now would find no CLI.\n\n**Decision:** I split step 1 into two specs, built in this order, because the request is too large for one:\n1. **`config-foundation`**: project setup, finding `troupe.yml`/`troupe.yaml`, loading with recursive `file:` includes, dotted paths, the `eventsourcing` event store with import on first command, `show`, `history`, and the exit-code and error rules. It records which file and position every value came from.\n2. **`config-set-writeback`**: `set PATH VALUE` with byte-surgical write-back: choosing the target file, quoting, block and folded values, comment columns, line endings and appends. It also records `set`/`remove` events and writes files atomically. It depends on the first spec.\n\nThe write-back rules are the riskiest part, so they get their own spec and review.\n\n**Approach chosen:** I made this choice myself rather than asking, since your brief was detailed. `ruamel.yaml` only parses the files; edits are applied as text patches at the recorded positions, and the whole file is never re-written from the parsed form. After each patch the file is re-parsed, and if the result isn't the intended config the write is refused with exit 3. I ruled out:\n- **Re-writing the file with ruamel:** it reformats parts nobody asked to change.\n- **PyYAML:** it reads values like `yes` as booleans (the wrong YAML version) and drops comments.\n- **A hand-written YAML parser:** too much work for step 1.\n\n**Check done:** `ruamel.yaml` 0.19.1 and `eventsourcing` 9.5.5 install together under Python 3.12. `ruamel` reports where each value sits in the file and how it's quoted, and reads `yes` as a string, as YAML 1.2 requires.\n\n**One open question for the design:** after the first import, hand edits are not added to history. The design must decide whether `show` reads the files or the stored projection, and record why. I've noted this in the roadmap and the `config-foundation` brief.\n\nFiles:\n- `spec/steering/roadmap.md`\n- `spec/spec/config-foundation/brief.md`\n- `spec/spec/config-set-writeback/brief.md`\n\n**Next step:** run `/method-command` to write both specs. Then `/method-command config-foundation`, then `/method-command config-set-writeback`, committing each on `main`. That is when the CLI will actually exist.

tool: Write {"content": "# Research & Design Decisions: config-foundation\n\n## Summary\n- **Feature**: `config-foundation`\n- **Discovery Scope**: New Feature (greenfield; full discovery)\n- **Key Findings**:\n  - ruamel.yaml 0.19.1 `compose()` gives every node a `start_mark.index` / `end_mark.index` that are **character\n    (code point) indices into the decoded text**, plus scalar style (`None` plain, `'`, `\"`, `|`, `>`) and\n    `flow_style` for collections. This is enough to build a source-mapped tree without ever re-dumping.\n  - ruamel's round-trip resolver is **not a strict YAML 1.2 core-schema resolver**: `1_0` resolves to int 10 and\n    `2001-12-14` to a timestamp, both of which are strings under the 1.2 core schema. The model therefore types\n    plain scalars with its own core-schema function and uses ruamel only for structure, positions and style.\n  - eventsourcing 9.5.5 with `PERSISTENCE_MODULE=eventsourcing.sqlite` passed through the `env` constructor\n    argument persists to a single SQLite file (plus `-wal`/`-shm` siblings), saves all pending events of one\n    aggregate in one transaction, and round-trips `str`, `int`, `float` (including `inf`), `bool` and `None`\n    unchanged. Explicit `env` overrides `os.environ`.\n\n## Research Log\n\n### ruamel.yaml composition, marks and styles\n- **Context**: The loader must record file, span, style and block/flow for every node (shared seam with\n  config-set-writeback).\n- **Sources Consulted**: Local probes against ruamel.yaml 0.19.1 on Python 3.12.14 (`/tmp` scratch project,\n  not committed); ruamel.yaml source (`composer.py`, `nodes.py`).\n- **Findings**:\n  - `YAML().compose(text)` returns `MappingNode` / `SequenceNode` / `ScalarNode` or `None` for an empty or\n    comment-only document.\n  - Indices are character indices: in `é: café\\r\\n` the value starts at index 3 after a one-character key.\n  - Scalar span text includes quotes and, for block scalars, the header and all content lines\n    (`'|\\r\\n  hi\...[truncated 12741 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "# Design Document: config-foundation\n\n## Overview\n**Purpose**: This feature delivers the read side of troupe's configuration subsystem: `troupe config show PATH`\nand `troupe config history [PATH]` over a theatre's hand-edited `.troupe/troupe.yml` (or `.yaml`) with recursive\n`file:` includes, plus the shared foundations that the downstream `set` command (config-set-writeback) builds on.\n\n**Users**: Developers who hand-edit and diff their theatre configuration use it to read single settings from the\nshell and to review the configuration's change history. The config-set-writeback spec uses its model, path\nresolution, history API and error types.\n\n**Impact**: Greenfield. Creates the Python package `troupe` (src layout, uv, console script `troupe`), the\n`troupe.config` core and file layer, and the `troupe.cli` layer, confirming the layout proposed in\n`structure.md`.\n\n### Goals\n- `show` and `history` behave exactly as the step 1 contract (General, Includes, show, history) states.\n- A source-mapped configuration model that records, for every node, its file, character span, style, block/flow\n  kind and include provenance, narrow enough for the byte-surgical writer to consume without re-parsing logic.\n- An eventsourcing-based history with one atomic import per theatre and an append API for `set`/`remove` events.\n- One error hierarchy and one exit-code mapping used by every subcommand; stdout empty on failure.\n\n### Non-Goals\n- `set`, VALUE parsing, write-target resolution, rendering and patching (config-set-writeback).\n- Deciding which leaves a `set` changed (config-set-writeback computes the diff with this spec's flattening).\n- Anchors/aliases/merge keys, multi-document files, explicit tags, concurrent writers, Windows.\n- A \"current value\" projection from events (no consumer; see decision \"Files are authoritative\").\n\n## Boundary Commitments\n\n### This Spec Owns\n- Project scaffold: `pyproject.toml`, uv lock, console script `troup...[truncated 42359 chars]

',line)\n    if cur and m: ids.append(f\"{cur}.{m.group(1)}\")\ncov=set()\nfor a,b,c in re.findall(r'(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)(?:[–-](?:\\d+\\.)?(\\d+))?',des):\n    lo=int(b); hi=int(c) if c else lo\n    for i in range(lo,hi+1): cov.add(f\"{a}.{i}\")\nprint(len(ids),'ids; missing:',[i for i in ids if i not in cov])\nEOF", "description": "Check requirement ID coverage in design"}
tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo/spec/spec/config-foundation; python3 - <<'EOF'\np='design.md'; t=open(p).read()\nold=\"- Atomic import: a store save that fails mid-import (forced via an unwritable store file) leaves no\\n  `HistoryStarted`, and the next successful run imports fully (7.7).\"\nnew=\"- Atomic import: a store-level test injects a failure at the external SQLite boundary (the recorder's insert\\n  raises after the first rows are written inside the transaction); afterwards `is_imported()` is False, no\\n  records exist, and the next `ensure_imported` records the complete import (7.7).\"\nassert old in t; t=t.replace(old,new)\nold2=\"- Any eventsourcing/SQLite failure while opening or reading → `ConfigLoadError(file=<theatre>/.troupe/history.sqlite)`.\"\nnew2=\"- Any eventsourcing/SQLite failure while opening, importing, recording or reading → `ConfigLoadError(file=<theatre>/.troupe/history.sqlite)`\\n  (exit 4). A failed write leaves the store unchanged (transaction rolled back). For `record_changes`, the caller\\n  (config-set-writeback) owns the ordering between its file write and the event write.\"\nassert old2 in t; t=t.replace(old2,new2)\nopen(p,'w').write(t)\nEOF\nwc -l design.md research.md requirements.md", "description": "Repair design draft after review"}

tool: Write {"content": "# Requirements Document\n\n## Project Description (Input)\n### Problem\nDevelopers review every change to their configuration as a diff. `troupe config set` must change a\nsetting in whichever file holds it, and change **only the bytes of that value**. Comments, quoting, layout,\nindentation, blank lines and line endings elsewhere must stay exactly as they were.\n\n### Current State\nconfig-foundation provides loading with includes into a source-mapped model, path resolution, the event\nstore/projection with import, and error/exit-code conventions. Nothing writes to the user's files yet.\n\n### Desired Outcome\n`uv run troupe config set PATH VALUE [--theatre DIR]` follows the step 1 contract section `set PATH VALUE`:\n- VALUE is parsed as a single YAML 1.2 core-schema flow node.\n- Target resolution: an existing value is changed in the file that contains it. A text-include target's\n  content becomes VALUE exactly, with CRLF preserved if the target used CRLF; a non-string VALUE → 3.\n  A new key goes into the file that holds the deepest existing ancestor mapping, and missing intermediate\n  mappings are created there. An index equal to a list's length appends; a larger index → 5. tool: Write {"content": "# Design Document: config-set-writeback\n\n## Overview\n**Purpose**: This feature delivers `troupe config set PATH VALUE`: it changes one setting of a theatre's\nconfiguration and writes the change back into the file that holds it, changing only the bytes the step 1\ncontract requires, and records the change as `set`/`remove` events in the configuration history.\n\n**Users**: Developers who hand-edit their theatre configuration and review every change as a diff use it to\nchange settings from the shell and scripts.\n\n**Impact**: Adds the `troupe.config.writeback` package (VALUE parsing, write-target resolution, text layout\nanalysis, renderers, patch planner, verification, leaf diff, atomic file writing, the set use case) and\nregisters the `set` subcommand in the existing CLI shell. config-foundation's modules are consumed unchanged\napart from one required upstream addition (fold markers, see \"Required Upstream Additions\").\n\n### Goals\n- Every rule of the contract section `set PATH VALUE` is implemented by one named function and proved by a\n  byte-exact test through the real CLI.\n- A successful set changes only required bytes; any doubt ends in exit 3 with no file changed.\n- The written configuration is proven, before writing, to equal the intended configuration by re-loading it\n  with the foundation loader.\n\n### Non-Goals\n- Loading, includes, path syntax and resolution, history storage/import/printing, error types (config-foundation).\n- Step 5's change of the new-key target rule; anchors/aliases/merge keys (step 6); multi-document files; TAB\n  before end-of-line comments; concurrent writers; Windows.\n- Creating new includes through `set` (refused, see 14.8); writing several files in one set (refused, 13.6).\n\n## Boundary Commitments\n\n### This Spec Owns\n- The `set` subcommand: its argparse subparser, handler and success behaviour (no output).\n- VALUE parsing into a typed, style-free value tree (`NewValue`).\n- Write-target resoluti...[truncated 48102 chars]

If it isn't the intended configuration, the command exits 3 and no file changes.\n- A `set` whose value starts with `file:` is written like any other string. If its target is missing or forms a cycle, it is refused with exit 3.\n- File writes go through a hidden temporary file next to the target, then an atomic rename. A hard kill mid-write could leave that temporary file behind.\n- Infinity and NaN appear in history as the JSON strings `".inf"`, `"-.inf"` and `".nan"`, so every line stays valid JSON.\n- A malformed path such as `a..b` exits 2. Duplicate keys, explicit tags, anchors and files that aren't UTF-8 exit 4.\n\n**One change from my own discovery plan:** the history is stored as SQLite at `.troupe/history.sqlite`, with its `-wal`/`-shm` side files also under `.troupe/`.\n\n**Next:** run `/method-command config-foundation`, then `/method-command config-set-writeback`, committing each on `main`.

tool: Bash {"command": "for d in config-foundation config-set-writeback; do python3 - \"$d\" <<'EOF'\nimport re,sys\nd=sys.argv[1]\nreq=open(f'{d}/requirements.md').read().split('## Requirements')[1]\nids=[]\ncur=None\nfor line in req.splitlines():\n    m=re.match(r'### Requirement (\\d+)',line)\n    if m: cur=m.group(1)\n    m=re.match(r'(\\d+)\\. ',line)\n    if m and cur: ids.append(f'{cur}.{m.group(1)}')\ndef expand(text):\n    out=set()\n    for a,b,c in re.findall(r'(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)(?:[–-](?:\\d+\\.)?(\\d+))?',text):\n        if c: out|={f'{a}.{i}' for i in range(int(b),int(c)+1)}\n        else: out.add(f'{a}.{b}')\n    for a in re.findall(r'(\\d+)\\.x',text): out|={i for i in ids if i.startswith(a+'.')}\n    return out\nt=open(f'{d}/tasks.md').read()\ntreq=set()\nfor m in re.findall(r'_Requirements: ([^_]*)_',t): treq|=expand(m)\ndes=open(f'{d}/design.md').read()\ntr=des.split('## Requirements Traceability')[1].split('## Components')[0]\ndreq=expand(tr)\nprint(d,len(ids),'missing in tasks:',[i for i in ids if i not in treq],'missing in design trace:',[i for i in ids if i not in dreq], 'unknown in tasks:',sorted(treq-set(ids)))\nEOF\ndone"}

assistant: I recorded all nine answers in both specs and committed them on `main` (`8c0725b`). **The CLI is still not built.** I stopped before implementation because `method-command` is set up so that only you can start it, not me.\n\n**What changed in the specs:**\n- **`show` and `set` read the files on disk (confirmed).** A hand edit shows up in `show` but records no history event. A later `set` records the value in the file as `old`. Tests for both are now in the task lists.\n- **A `set` that touches several files now goes ahead instead of being refused.** This was your call to me, and I reversed my earlier choice. The contract's "only bytes that differ in any file" plus rule 1 means replacing a collection that contains a text include must legitimately change two files, so refusing would contradict it. To keep data safe:\n  - Every file's patch is built and checked in memory before anything is written.\n  - If a later write fails, the earlier files are restored to their original bytes and the command exits 3 with no history recorded.\n  - A change that would alter the configuration anywhere other than at PATH, such as a file included in two places, is still refused.\n- **A `file:` value is kept as a plain string.** If its target is missing or forms a cycle, the command exits 3 and no file changes. This never leaves you with a configuration that can't load.\n- **No leftover files.** Tests now check that no extra file remains after success or after any failure. The history store is closed at the end of every command, and nothing may appear outside `.troupe/`.\n- **Kept as before, with reasons recorded:**\n  - Infinity and NaN in history are written as `".inf"`, `"-.inf"` and `".nan"`.\n  - A malformed path such as `a..b` exits 2.\n  - Anchors, aliases, merge keys, duplicate keys, explicit tags and files that aren't UTF-8 all exit 4.\n\n**One trade-off to know about:** if restoring a file after a failed write itself fails, the command keeps its original exit code and names every file it couldn't restore. That breaks the usual meaning of exit 3 ("no file changed"), but only in a case the contract doesn't define.\n\nEach decision is recorded with its reason in the specs' `research.md`, with a summary in `spec/steering/roadmap.md`.\n\n**Next:** run `/method-command config-foundation`, then `/method-command config-set-writeback`. Each task gets an implementer and an independent reviewer, and is committed on `main`.

This module is pure data:\nit performs no I/O. All dataclasses are frozen and all collections are tuples. Node values are the\ntrue YAML values (plain built-ins only; folded ``>`` scalars are folded with no U+0007 markers),\nwhile ``SourceFile.text`` and every span are left exactly as the file was read.\n\nSpan semantics\n--------------\n* ``Span.start`` (inclusive) and ``Span.end`` (exclusive) are **character (code point) indices**\n  into ``SourceFile.text``, the exact decoded file text (UTF-8, no newline translation, BOM kept).\n  A byte offset, when needed, is ``len(text[:i].encode(\"utf-8\"))``.\n* Plain and quoted scalar spans are exact; quoted spans cover the quotes.\n* A block scalar's span starts at its indicator (``|`` or ``>``, with any chomping/indentation\n  indicators) and covers the header line and all content lines including the final line break, but\n  it may also extend over trailing blank lines (for ``'|\\\\n  a\\\\n  b\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n'`` the value is\n  ``'a\\\\nb\\\\n'`` and the span covers all the trailing blank lines). A block scalar's ``end`` is\n  therefore not tight.\n* The span of an empty (zero-length) null value (e.g. ``key:`` with nothing after it) is not a\n  reliable position; consumers must not patch at it.\n* Mapping and sequence spans are as reported by the composer. Flow collection spans are exact\n  (``[`` ... ``]``, ``{`` ... ``}``). tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > src/troupe/config/locate.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Locate the root configuration file of a theatre (Requirements 2.1-2.4).\n\nOnly checks existence: nothing is created, opened or modified here.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom troupe.config.constants import CONFIG_DIR_NAME, CONFIG_FILE_NAMES\nfrom troupe.config.errors import ConfigLoadError\n\n\ndef find_config_file(theatre_dir: Path) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Return ``<theatre_dir>/.troupe/<name>`` for the single existing regular config file.\n\n    Raises :class:`ConfigLoadError` naming the expected ``troupe.yml`` when no config file exists\n    (also when ``theatre_dir`` is missing or not a directory), and naming both files when both\n    ``troupe.yml`` and ``troupe.yaml`` exist.\n    \"\"\"\n    config_dir = theatre_dir / CONFIG_DIR_NAME\n    candidates = [config_dir / name for name in CONFIG_FILE_NAMES]\n    existing = [candidate for candidate in candidates if candidate.is_file()]\n    if not existing:\n        expected = \" or \".join(CONFIG_FILE_NAMES)\n        raise ConfigLoadError(\n            f\"no configuration file (expected {expected})\",\n            file=candidates[0],\n        )\n    if len(existing) > 1:\n        raise ConfigLoadError(\n            f\"both {existing[0].name} and {existing[1]} exist\",\n            file=existing[0],\n        )\n    return existing[0]\nEOF\nuv run pytest 2>&1 | tail -2; uv run mypy --strict . ; uv run ruff check . ; uv run ruff format --check .; git status --short"}

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"Loading a single YAML file into the source-mapped model (Requirements 3.1-3.9).\n\nEvery test writes real YAML into a temporary theatre and loads it with ``load_config``. Span tests\ncheck ruamel's marks empirically: ``text[span]`` must be the exact written source.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport hashlib\nimport math\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom support import MakeTheatre\nfrom troupe.config.errors import ConfigLoadError, ExitCode\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.model import (\n    CollectionStyle,\n    ConfigDocument,\n    ConfigMapping,\n    ConfigNode,\n    ConfigScalar,\n    ConfigSequence,\n    LineEnding,\n    MappingEntry,\n    ScalarStyle,\n    Span,\n)\n\n# A fixture with comments, blank lines, unusual key order, quoted keys, multibyte characters,\n# every scalar style and both collection styles.\nRICH = \"\"\"\\\n# leading comment\nzeta: plain value   # trailing comment\n'single key': 'it''s'\n\"double key\": \"tab\\\\there\"\né: café\n\nunicode: \"😀 ünï\"\ncount: 0o17\ntruth: yes\nnothing:\ntilde: ~\nlist:\n  - 1\n  - \"two\"\n  - [1, yes, 0.1, null, ~, 1e3]\nflow: {a: 1, 'b': x}\nliteral: |\n  line one\n  line two\nstrip: |-\n  kept\nfold: >\n  folded\n  text\n\nnested:\n  inner: 'q'   # comment after\n  multi: plain\n    continued\nlast: 1_0\n\"\"\"\n\n# (key path, exact span text, style, value) for every plain and quoted scalar value in RICH.\nRICH_SCALARS: list[tuple[tuple[str | int, ...], str, ScalarStyle, object]] = [\n    ((\"zeta\",), \"plain value\", ScalarStyle.PLAIN, \"plain value\"),\n    ((\"single key\",), \"'it''s'\", ScalarStyle.SINGLE_QUOTED, \"it's\"),\n    ((\"double key\",), '\"tab\\\\there\"', ScalarStyle.DOUBLE_QUOTED, \"tab\\there\"),\n    ((\"é\",), \"café\", ScalarStyle.PLAIN, \"café\"),\n    ((\"unicode\",), '\"😀 ünï\"', ScalarStyle.DOUBLE_QUOTED, \"😀 ünï\"),\n    ((\"count\",), \"0o17\", ScalarStyle.PLAIN, 15),\n    ((\"truth\",), \"yes\", ScalarStyle.PLAIN, \"yes\"),\...[truncated 20489 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"Load the configuration into the source-mapped model (Requirements 3.1-3.9).\n\nThe loader is the only reader of the user's configuration files. It reads bytes read-only,\ndecodes them strictly as UTF-8 without newline translation (so a leading BOM and every CRLF are\nkept), composes exactly one YAML document with ruamel.yaml's round-trip composer and builds the\nimmutable model of :mod:`troupe.config.model` from the composed nodes.\n\nruamel.yaml is used only for structure, positions (``start_mark.index``/``end_mark.index`` are\ncharacter indices into the composed text) and styles. Plain scalars are typed with\n:func:`troupe.config.scalars.resolve_plain_scalar` (YAML 1.2 core schema); quoted and block\nscalars are strings. Folded (``>``) values have the U+0007 fold markers that the round-trip\ncomposer inserts removed (3.8).\n\nUnsupported YAML is refused with :class:`ConfigLoadError` naming the file and, where known, the\nkey path (product-owner decisions H and I): non-UTF-8 bytes, syntax errors, several documents,\nduplicate keys, explicit tags, anchors, aliases (a defined alias is caught by its anchor, which\ncomes first in the document; an undefined one is a composer error), plain ``<<`` merge keys,\nnon-scalar keys and a top-level node that is not a mapping. An empty or comment-only file is an\nempty block mapping at ``Span(0, 0)``.\n\nNothing is ever created, modified, renamed or deleted (3.6).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Final\n\nfrom ruamel.yaml import YAML\nfrom ruamel.yaml.error import MarkedYAMLError, YAMLError\nfrom ruamel.yaml.nodes import MappingNode, Node, ScalarNode, SequenceNode\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import ConfigLoadError\nfrom troupe.config.model import (\n    CollectionStyle,\n    ConfigDocument,\n    ConfigMapping,\n    ConfigNode,\n    ConfigScalar,\n    ConfigSequence,\n    LineEnding,\n    MappingEntry,\n    Origin,\n    ScalarStyle,\n    SourceFile,\n ...[truncated 11648 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"Event-sourced configuration history: aggregate, events and records (7.1, 7.3, 7.5, 9.1, 9.2).\n\nOne :class:`ConfigHistory` aggregate with the fixed identity :data:`HISTORY_AGGREGATE_ID` records\nthe history of one theatre. Its events are totally ordered by version: the created event\n:class:`ConfigHistory.HistoryStarted` is version 1 and marks the theatre as imported (it is not a\nhistory line), and every later event is one history line whose ``seq`` is its version minus one,\nso ``seq`` starts at 1 and has no gaps.\n\nThe aggregate holds no derived leaf state: the files are the truth for current values, and the\nhistory is change history only. Persistence lives in ``troupe.config.store``, which projects stored\nevents through :func:`to_history_record`, the single home of the event-to-record mapping.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Final, Literal, TypeAlias\nfrom uuid import NAMESPACE_URL, UUID, uuid5\n\nfrom eventsourcing.domain import Aggregate, event\n\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.scalars import ScalarValue\n\nHISTORY_AGGREGATE_ID: Final[UUID] = uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, \"troupe:config-history\")\n\"\"\"The fixed identity of the one history aggregate in every theatre's store.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass ConfigHistory(Aggregate):\n    \"\"\"The history of one theatre; event class names are the single home of event names.\"\"\"\n\n    @classmethod\n    def create_id(cls) -> UUID:  # type: ignore[override]\n        # The library declares ``create_id(*_: Any, **__: Any)`` and passes it only the keyword\n        # arguments named in this signature (none here); the fixed ID makes the history unique.\n        return HISTORY_AGGREGATE_ID\n\n    class HistoryStarted(Aggregate.Created):\n        \"\"\"The theatre's configuration was imported (version 1); not a history line.\"\"\"\n\n    class LeafImported(Aggregate.Event):\n        \"\"\"A leaf found at import time: op ``import``, ``old`` null.\"\"\"\...[truncated 2929 chars]

Every eventsourcing/SQLite failure is reported as a :class:`ConfigLoadError`\nnaming the store file. :meth:`HistoryStore.close` closes every SQLite connection, after which SQLite\ncheckpoints the write-ahead log and removes the side files.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sqlite3\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Self, TypeVar\nfrom uuid import UUID\n\nfrom eventsourcing.application import Application\nfrom eventsourcing.domain import EventSourcingError\nfrom eventsourcing.utils import Environment, TopicError\n\nfrom troupe.config.constants import HISTORY_STORE_NAME\nfrom troupe.config.errors import ConfigLoadError\nfrom troupe.config.history import (\n    HISTORY_AGGREGATE_ID,\n    ConfigHistory,\n    HistoryRecord,\n    to_history_record,\n)\nfrom troupe.config.resolve import Leaf\n\n_T = TypeVar(\"_T\")\n\n# Failures of the store itself: SQLite errors (some escape eventsourcing unwrapped, e.g. when the\n# file is not a database), eventsourcing's persistence/topic errors, file-system errors, and\n# decoding errors from corrupt stored state (``json.JSONDecodeError`` is a ``ValueError``).\n_STORE_FAILURES = (sqlite3.Error, EventSourcingError, TopicError, OSError, ValueError)\n\n\nclass _HistoryApplication(Application[UUID]):\n    \"\"\"The eventsourcing application holding the sing...[truncated 4758 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"The theatre session: use cases shared by every subcommand (6.1-6.9, 7.4, 7.9, 8.3-8.5).\n\nA command opens its theatre with ``with open_theatre(directory) as theatre:``. Opening follows a\nfixed order: locate the configuration file, load it from disk, open the history store, import the\nconfiguration once. Nothing is created when locating or loading fails (7.4). Leaving the ``with``\nblock closes the history store, whether the block succeeded or failed (7.9).\n\nFiles are the truth (product-owner decision A): ``theatre.document`` is the configuration as read\nfrom disk by this command, :func:`show_value` reads only that document, and the history is change\nhistory only. A hand edit made since the import is shown and never recorded (6.9, 7.3).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom types import TracebackType\nfrom typing import Self\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import ConfigLoadError, WrongNodeKindError\nfrom troupe.config.history import HistoryRecord\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.locate import find_config_file\nfrom troupe.config.model import ConfigDocument, ConfigMapping, ConfigScalar\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath, path_has_prefix\nfrom troupe.config.resolve import flatten_leaves, resolve_path\nfrom troupe.config.scalars import ScalarValue\nfrom troupe.config.store import HistoryStore\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Theatre:\n    \"\"\"An opened theatre: its configuration as on disk and its (imported) history store.\"\"\"\n\n    directory: Path\n    config_file: Path\n    document: ConfigDocument  # the files as on disk when the command opened the theatre\n    history: HistoryStore\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Close the history store; calling it again does nothing.\"\"\"\n        self.history.close()\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> Self:\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(\n        self,\n        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,\...[truncated 2612 chars]

tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; python3 - <<'EOF'\np='tests/test_theatre.py'; s=open(p).read()\nanchor=\"# --- show_value\"\nadd='''def test_exit_with_exception_info_never_raises_a_close_error_even_with_no_active_exception(\n    theatre_dir: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch\n) -> None:\n    # ``__exit__`` may be called (e.g. by an exit stack) when no exception is active; the\n    # exception info it receives, not ``sys.exception()``, decides that the body failed.\n    theatre = open_theatre(theatre_dir)\n    _failing_application_close(monkeypatch)\n    body_error = KeyError(\"original\")\n\n    suppress = theatre.__exit__(KeyError, body_error, None)\n\n    assert not suppress\n    assert _store_files(theatre_dir) == [HISTORY_STORE_NAME]\n\n\n'''\ns=s.replace(anchor, add+anchor,1); open(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\npython3 - <<'EOF'\np='src/troupe/config/theatre.py'; s=open(p).read()\ns=s.replace(\"        if exc_type is None:\\n            self.close()\\n            return\\n        try:\\n            self.close()\\n        except ConfigLoadError:\\n            pass  # the block's own error is the one reported\\n\",\"        self.close()\\n\")\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\nuv run pytest tests/test_theatre.py -q 2>&1 | tail -6; cp /tmp/t.py src/troupe/config/theatre.py; uv run pytest tests/test_theatre.py -q 2>&1 | tail -2"}

a valid core-schema hex integer far beyond 4300 decimal digits\n\n\ndef _decimal_digits(value: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decimal text of ``value`` computed independently of ``str`` (and its digit limit).\"\"\"\n    digits = []\n    rest = abs(value)\n    while True:\n        rest, digit = divmod(rest, 10)\n        digits.append(\"0123456789\"[digit])\n        if rest == 0:\n            break\n    return (\"-\" if value < 0 else \"\") + \"\".join(reversed(digits))\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"value\", \"expected\"),\n    [\n        (\"hello\", b\"hello\\n\"),\n        (\"hello\\n\", b\"hello\\n\"),\n        (\"two\\nlines\", b\"two\\nlines\\n\"),\n        (\"crlf\\r\\n\", b\"crlf\\r\\n\"),\n        (\"cr only\\r\", b\"cr only\\r\\n\"),\n        (\"\", b\"\\n\"),\n        (\"\\n\", b\"\\n\"),\n        (\"ends twice\\n\\n\", b\"ends twice\\n\\n\"),\n        (\"café ☃\", \"café ☃\\n\".encode()),\n        (\"true\", b\"true\\n\"),\n        (True, b\"true\\n\"),\n        (False, b\"false\\n\"),\n        (None, b\"null\\n\"),\n        (0, b\"0\\n\"),\n        (42, b\"42\\n\"),\n        (-7, b\"-7\\n\"),\n        (255, b\"255\\n\"),\n        (0.2, b\"0.2\\n\"),\n        (1.0, b\"1.0\\n\"),\n       ...[truncated 4404 chars]

The user's\nfiles are never modified (3.6 is proven in full by the read-only safety tests).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom support import CliResult, MakeTheatre, RunCli\n\nCONFIG_NAMES = [\"troupe.yml\", \"troupe.yaml\"]\n\n# Both read commands share the locate/load conventions (10.5).\nCOMMANDS = [(\"show\", \"a\"), (\"history\",)]\n\n\ndef _assert_load_failure(result: CliResult, file: Path, path: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Assert exit 4, empty stdout and a single stderr line naming ``file`` (and ``path``).\n\n    Returns the problem text that follows the file (and path) prefix.\n    \"\"\"\n    prefix = f\"{file}: \" if path is None else f\"{file}: {path}: \"\n    assert result.exit_code == 4, result.stderr\n    assert result.stdout == b\"\"\n    assert result.stderr.startswith(prefix), result.stderr\n    assert result.stderr.endswith(\"\\n\")\n    assert result.stderr.count(\"\\n\") == 1, result.stderr\n    return result.stderr[len(prefix) :]\n\n\ndef _snapshot(root: Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:\n    \"\"\"Every regular file under ``root`` (relative path -> bytes).\"\"\"\n    return {\n        str(entry.relative_to(root)): entry.read_bytes()\n        for entry in sorted(root.rglob(\"*\"))\n        if entry.is_file()\n    }\n\n\n# ---- 2.1, 1.2: exactly one of troupe.yml / troupe.yaml is used ----\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"config_name\", CONFIG_NAMES)\ndef test_show_reads_the_single_existing_config_file(\n    make_theatre: MakeTheatre, run_cli: RunCli, config_name: str\n) -> None:\n    theatre = make_theatre(f\"a: from {config...[truncated 9740 chars]

assistant: config-foundation is built and committed on `main`, and the final validation result is **GO**. `uv run troupe config show PATH` and `uv run troupe config history [PATH]` now work from the repository root. **`set` does not exist yet**; it belongs to the second spec.\n\n**Checks, run fresh on the final commit:** 724 tests pass, and `mypy --strict`, ruff lint and ruff format are clean. `uv run troupe config --help` and real `show`/`history` runs against a sample theatre behave correctly. The validator also ran about 40 of its own probes against the contract, and all passed:\n- Missing, duplicate or unloadable config files exit 4.\n- A mapping, a list or a missing path exits 5.\n- A text include prints byte for byte, including CRLF.\n- History lines are strict JSON with `seq` counting from 1.\n- A hand edit shows in `show` but adds no history event.\n- After each command the only state is `.troupe/history.sqlite`, and user files keep identical bytes.\n\n**How the run went:** all 20 sub-tasks went through implementer → independent reviewer → fresh checks → one commit each, from `e6d5ee7` to `0502077`. One review rejected a change: task 5.2 had added large-number handling for a case the history store already blocks, so it was simplified back to the design. I asked for one fix before review: an empty PATH used to print a message starting with ": ". No task was blocked. Every module the `set` spec builds on exists with the agreed signatures.\n\n**Two problems to handle in `set`.** I've written both into config-set-writeback's implementation notes:\n- **Values starting with `-`:** the argument parser treats `-1e3`, `-.inf` or `-x` as options and exits 2. Plain `-1` and `-0.5` work.\n- **A type annotation that would crash the CLI:** copied as written from the `set` design, it fails when the module loads on Python 3.12, which would break every command. It needs to be quoted, as in `main.py`.\n\n**Choices to know about:**\n- `--theatre` is only accepted after the subcommand, as in the contract's `troupe config <subcommand> --theatre <dir>`.\n- A file containing only `---` or `~` exits 4 rather than counting as an empty configuration.\n- YAML allows a tab right after `key:`, but the parser we use (`ruamel.yaml`) rejects it, so such a file exits 4.\n\n**Housekeeping:** `spec.json` still says `tasks-generated`, and `spec/steering/structure.md` still says no code exists. The full test suite takes about 95 seconds because the end-to-end tests run the real CLI in subprocesses.\n\n**Next:** run `/method-command config-set-writeback` (32 tasks) to build `set`.

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"ValueParser: the typed, style-free value tree of a VALUE given to ``troupe config set``.\n\nThe parsed-value types live here so that the parser and the plain-tree module share them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import TypeAlias\n\nfrom troupe.config.scalars import ScalarValue\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass NewScalar:\n    \"\"\"A scalar of VALUE: its typed value and, for non-strings, the plain text it was written as.\"\"\"\n\n    value: ScalarValue\n    spelling: str | None\n    \"\"\"Source text for ``int``/``float``/``bool``/``None`` (e.g. ``0x1F``); ``None`` for strings.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass NewMapping:\n    \"\"\"A flow mapping of VALUE; entries keep VALUE order.\"\"\"\n\n    entries: tuple[tuple[str, \"NewValue\"], ...]\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass NewSequence:\n    \"\"\"A flow list of VALUE.\"\"\"\n\n    items: tuple[\"NewValue\", ...]\n\n\n# A runtime union (not a ``type`` statement) so callers can also use it with ``isinstance``.\nNewValue: TypeAlias = NewScalar | NewMapping | NewSequence  # noqa: UP040\n\"\"\"One node of a parsed VALUE.\"\"\"\n", "file_path": "/work/repo/src/troupe/config/writeback/value.py"}

tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > /tmp/probe.py <<'EOF'\nimport sys, tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.model import *\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.layout import FileLayout\n\ndef setup(text):\n    d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); p = d/\"troupe.yml\"; p.write_bytes(text.encode())\n    doc = load_config(p); return FileLayout.build(doc.root_file, doc), doc, text\n\ndef node(doc, *segs):\n    n = doc.root\n    for s in segs:\n        n = n.items[s] if isinstance(s,int) else n.get(s).value\n    return n\n\ndef ip(text, *segs):\n    try:\n        lay, doc, t = setup(text)\n        p = lay.insertion_point(node(doc,*segs))\n        print(repr(text), segs, \"->\", p, repr(t[:p.index]) [-30:], \"|\", repr(t[p.index:])[:30])\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(repr(text), segs, \"EXC\", type(e).__name__, e)\n\ndef cm(text):\n    try:\n        lay, doc, t = setup(text)\n        for i in range(lay.line_count):\n            c = lay.comment_start(i)\n            print(i, repr(lay.line_text(i)), c, None if c is None else repr(t[c:c+5]))\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(repr(text), \"EXC\", type(e).__name__, e)\n\nexec(open(sys.argv[1]).read())\nEOF\ncat > /tmp/p1.py <<'EOF'\nprint(\"== comments\")\ncm(\"key: 'a#b' # c\\n\")\ncm(\"key: a#b # c\\n\")\ncm(\"key: \\\"it's # x\\\" # c 'q' \\\"z\\n\")\ncm(\"key: a\\n  b # c\\n\")\ncm(\"key: a # c\\n\")\ncm(\"k: {a: 1,\\n  b: 2} # c\\n\")\ncm(\"k: [a, 'b # x',\\n  c] # c\\n\")\ncm(\"k: |\\n  # not comment\\n  x\\n# real\\n\")\ncm(\"k: x\\r\\n# y\\r\\nz: 'a#' #c\\r\\n\")\ncm(\"- a # c\\n- 'b#' # d\\n-   # e\\n\")\ncm(\"k:\\n  - x #c\\n  -\\n    a: 1 # c\\n\")\ncm(\"k: a  #c\\n\")\ncm(\"k: a\\t# c\\n\")\ncm(\"'k # z': v # c\\n\")\ncm(\"k: !!str a # c\\n\")\ncm(\"k: &x a # c\\nj: *x # d\\n\")\nEOF\nuv run python /tmp/probe.py /tmp/p1.py 2>&1", "description": "Probe comment detection"}

tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > /tmp/p3.py <<'EOF'\ndef ce(text, *segs):\n    lay, doc, t = setup(text)\n    parent = node(doc, *segs[:-1]); \n    from troupe.config.model import ConfigMapping\n    if isinstance(parent, ConfigMapping):\n        e = parent.get(segs[-1]); s = lay.entry_slot(parent, e, ConfigPath(()) if False else None)\n    else:\n        s = lay.item_slot(parent, segs[-1], None)\n    n = s.node\n    end = lay.content_end(n, s)\n    print(repr(text), segs, \"span\", n.origin.span, \"end\", end, repr(t[:end])[-25:], \"| ext\", lay.inline_extent(s), \"body\", lay.body_lines(s))\nfor t in [\"a:\\n  b:\\n    c: |+\\n      x\\n  # mid\\nd: 1\\n\",\n          \"a:\\n  b:\\n    c: |+\\n      x\\n\\n  # mid\\n\\nd: 1\\n\",\n          \"a:\\n  b:\\n    c: |\\n      x\\n\\n  # mid\\n\\nd: 1\\n\",\n          \"a:\\n  b:\\n    c: |+\\n      x\\n    \\n  # mid\\n\"]:\n    ce(t, \"a\",\"b\",\"c\")\n    ip(t, \"a\", \"b\")\n    cm(t)\nce(\"a: |+\\n  x\\n\\n\", \"a\")\nce(\"a: |+\\n  x\\n\\n  \", \"a\")\nce(\"a: |2-\\n   x\\n  \\n\", \"a\")\nce(\"a: plain\\n  multi # c\\n\", \"a\")\nce(\"a: {x: 1,\\n  y: 2}  # c\\nb: 1\\n\", \"a\")\nce(\"a: [\\n  1,\\n  2\\n]\\n\", \"a\")\nEOF\nuv run python /tmp/probe.py /tmp/p3.py 2>&1", "description": "Probe keep block scalars and extents"}

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"Unit tests of the EditApplier (``troupe.config.writeback.edits``): application of text edits in\nposition order, refusal of overlapping edits, and the end-of-line comment column fix-up.\n\nTraceability: every test names the requirement IDs it proves at the start of its docstring.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import WriteRefusedError\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.edits import EditKind, TextEdit, apply_edits\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.layout import FileLayout\n\n\ndef _layout(tmp_path: Path, config: str | bytes) -> FileLayout:\n    target = tmp_path / \"troupe.yml\"\n    target.write_bytes(config.encode(\"utf-8\") if isinstance(config, str) else config)\n    document = load_config(target)\n    return FileLayout.build(document.root_file, document)\n\n\ndef _replace(layout: FileLayout, old: str, new: str, *, occurrence: int = 0) -> TextEdit:\n    \"\"\"An INLINE edit replacing the ``occurrence``-th appearance of ``old`` with ``new``.\"\"\"\n    text = layout.file.text\n    start = -1\n    for _ in range(occurrence + 1):\n        start = text.index(old, start + 1)\n    return TextEdit(start, start + len(old), new, EditKind.INLINE)\n\n\ndef _apply(tmp_path: Path, config: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:\n    layout = _layout(tmp_path, config)\n    return apply_edits(layout, [_replace(layout, old, new)])\n\n\n# --- comment columns -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_longer_value_moves_comment_back_to_its_column(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Req 12.1: a longer value keeps the comment at its previous column.\"\"\"\n    assert _apply(tmp_path, \"a: 1    # c\\n\", \"1\", \"100\") == \"a: 100  # c\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_shorter_value_moves_comment_back_to_its_column(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Req 12.1: a shorter value keeps the comment at its previous column.\"\"\"\n    assert _apply(tmp_path,...[truncated 8677 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"EditApplier: text edits on one file, non-overlap check, application, comment-column fix-up.\n\nEdits are character (code point) ranges on one file's original text. They are applied in position\norder; overlapping edits are a planner bug and refused with :class:`WriteRefusedError` (14.9).\nAfter INLINE edits, each end-of-line comment on a line holding the end of such an edit is moved back\nto its original column, separated from the value by exactly one space when the value reaches that\ncolumn (12.1, 12.2). Columns are counted in code points (12.3); no other line is touched (12.4).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Final\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import WriteRefusedError\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.layout import FileLayout\n\n_BOM: Final = \"﻿\"\n_LINE_BREAKS: Final = \"\\r\\n\"\n\n_FLAG_ON: Final = False\n\n\nclass EditKind(Enum):\n    \"\"\"Whether an edit stays within line content or works on whole lines.\"\"\"\n\n    INLINE = \"inline\"  # replaces characters within line content; triggers comment fix-up\n    LINES = \"lines\"  # inserts or deletes whole lines; never triggers comment fix-up\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass TextEdit:\n    \"\"\"Replace ``[start, end)`` of a file's original text with ``text`` (``start == end`` inserts).\"\"\"\n\n    start: int\n    end: int\n    text: str\n    kind: EditKind\n\n\ndef apply_edits(layout: FileLayout, edits: Sequence[TextEdit]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the text of ``layout``'s file with ``edits`` applied and comment columns restored.\n\n    Edits are sorted by position; at equal positions insertions come before a replacement starting\n    there and otherwise the planner's order is kept. Raises :class:`WriteRefusedError` for an edit\n    outside the text or for overlapping edits.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = layout.file.text\n    ordered = sorted(edits, key=lambda edit: (edit.start, edit.end))\n    if _FLAG...[truncated 2899 chars]

tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > /tmp/rev_t.py <<'EOF'\nimport tempfile, pathlib\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.edits import EditKind, TextEdit, apply_edits\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.layout import FileLayout\ndef run(cfg, old, new):\n    d=pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); p=d/\"troupe.yml\"; p.write_bytes(cfg.encode())\n    doc=load_config(p); L=FileLayout.build(doc.root_file, doc)\n    s=cfg.index(old)\n    return apply_edits(L,[TextEdit(s,s+len(old),new,EditKind.INLINE)])\nfor c,o,n in [(\"a: 1\\t# c\\n\",\"1\",\"2\"),(\"a: 1\\t# c\\n\",\"1\",\"100\"),(\"a: 1 \\t # c\\n\",\"1\",\"2\"),\n              ('a: \"x\\n  y\"   # c\\nb: 1\\n','\"x\\n  y\"','\"xy\"'),('a: \"xy\"  # c\\n','\"xy\"','\"x\\n  y\"'),\n              (\"a: 1    # c\\n\",\"1\",\"2\")]:\n    print(repr(c),'->',repr(run(c,o,n)))\nEOF\nuv run python /tmp/rev_t.py"}

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"Unit tests of the ScalarRender (``troupe.config.writeback.scalar_render``): plain and\nsingle-quoted representability, style choice and fallback, double-quoted escaping, keys.\n\nEvery rendering that is meant to be written into a file is re-loaded with the real loader\n(``load_config``) in its context to prove it reads back as the intended value.\n\nTraceability: every test names the requirement IDs it proves at the start of its docstring.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import ExitCode, WriteRefusedError\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.model import ConfigMapping, ConfigScalar, ConfigSequence, ScalarStyle\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.scalars import ScalarValue\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.scalar_render import (\n    Context,\n    QuoteStyle,\n    can_represent,\n    choose_style,\n    quote_style_of,\n    render_key,\n    render_scalar,\n)\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import NewScalar\n\nPLAIN = ScalarStyle.PLAIN\nSINGLE = ScalarStyle.SINGLE_QUOTED\nDOUBLE = ScalarStyle.DOUBLE_QUOTED\nQUOTE_STYLES: tuple[QuoteStyle, ...] = (PLAIN, SINGLE, DOUBLE)\nPATH = ConfigPath.parse(\"agents.coder.model\")\n\n# Each context with the file texts that place a rendering ``{r}`` there.\nVALUE_PLACEMENTS: dict[Context, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    Context.BLOCK_VALUE: (\"k: {r}\\n\", \"l:\\n  - {r}\\n\", \"m:\\n  n: {r}  # c\\n\"),\n    Context.FLOW_VALUE: (\"k: [{r}, x]\\n\", \"k: {{a: {r}, b: x}}\\n\"),\n}\nKEY_PLACEMENTS: dict[Context, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    Context.BLOCK_KEY: (\"{r}: v\\n\", \"m:\\n  {r}: v  # c\\n\"),\n    Context.FLOW_KEY: (\"k: {{{r}: v, z: w}}\\n\",),\n}\n\n\ndef _load_root(tmp_path: Path, text: str) -> ConfigMapping:\n    target = tmp_path / \"troupe.yml\"\n    target.write_bytes(text.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    return load_config(target).root\n\n\ndef _first_value(root: ConfigMapping) -> ConfigScalar:\n    node = root...[truncated 18668 chars]
tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; python3 - <<'EOF'\np='tests/writeback/test_scalar_render.py'\ns=open(p).read()\nold_start=s.index('def _first_key(')\nold_end=s.index('def _reloaded_values(')\ns=s[:old_start]+'''def _first_key(root: ConfigMapping, nested: bool) -> str:\n    entry = root.entries[0]\n    if nested:\n        assert isinstance(entry.value, ConfigMapping)\n        entry = entry.value.entries[0]\n    return entry.key\n\n\n'''+s[old_end:]\ns=s.replace('''KEY_PLACEMENTS: dict[Context, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    Context.BLOCK_KEY: (\"{r}: v\\\\n\", \"m:\\\\n  {r}: v  # c\\\\n\"),\n    Context.FLOW_KEY: (\"k: {{{r}: v, z: w}}\\\\n\",),\n}''','''# Key placements: (file text, whether the key is nested one level below the root).\nKEY_PLACEMENTS: dict[Context, tuple[tuple[str, bool], ...]] = {\n    Context.BLOCK_KEY: ((\"{r}: v\\\\n\", False), (\"m:\\\\n  {r}: v  # c\\\\n\", True)),\n    Context.FLOW_KEY: ((\"k: {{{r}: v, z: w}}\\\\n\", True),),\n}''')\ns=s.replace('''        _first_key(_load_root(tmp_path, template.format(r=rendered)))\n        for template in KEY_PLACEMENTS[context]''','''        _first_key(_load_root(tmp_path, template.format(r=rendered)), nested)\n        for template, nested in KEY_PLACEMENTS[context]''')\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ngrep -n \"KEY_PLACEMENTS\\|_first_key\" tests/writeback/test_scalar_render.py; uv run pytest tests/writeback/test_scalar_render.py -q 2>&1 | tail -15"}
tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > src/troupe/config/writeback/scalar_render.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"ScalarRender: representability, style choice, plain/single/double scalar and key rendering.\"\"\"\n\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Literal, TypeAlias\n\nfrom troupe.config.model import ScalarStyle\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import NewScalar\n\n_ENABLED = False\n\n\nclass Context(Enum):\n    BLOCK_VALUE = \"block-value\"\n    FLOW_VALUE = \"flow-value\"\n    BLOCK_KEY = \"block-key\"\n    FLOW_KEY = \"flow-key\"\n\n\nQuoteStyle: TypeAlias = Literal[  # noqa: UP040\n    ScalarStyle.PLAIN, ScalarStyle.SINGLE_QUOTED, ScalarStyle.DOUBLE_QUOTED\n]\n\n\ndef can_represent(style: QuoteStyle, text: str, context: Context) -> bool:\n    raise NotImplementedError\n\n\ndef choose_style(value: str, context: Context, preferred: QuoteStyle | None) -> QuoteStyle:\n    raise NotImplementedError\n\n\ndef render_scalar(\n    value: NewScalar, context: Context, preferred: QuoteStyle | None, path: ConfigPath\n) -> str:\n    raise NotImplementedError\n\n\ndef render_key(\n    key: str, context: Context, preferred: QuoteStyle | None, *, path: ConfigPath | None = None\n) -> str:\n    raise NotImplementedError\n\n\ndef quote_style_of(style: ScalarStyle | None) -> QuoteStyle | None:\n    raise NotImplementedError\nEOF\nuv run pytest tests/writeback/test_scalar_render.py -q 2>&1 | tail -8"}
tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"ScalarRender: representability, style choice, plain/single/double scalar and key rendering.\n\nA string is written in a *quote style*: plain, single-quoted or double-quoted. The style of an\nexisting scalar (or of the preceding sibling of a new one) is kept when it can represent the new\ntext; otherwise the minimal style is used: plain if possible, otherwise single-quoted, otherwise\ndouble-quoted, which can represent every string.\n\nPlain representability is decided by a cheap syntactic check followed by a parse probe: the text is\nplaced in a tiny document of the exact context (block value, flow value, block key, flow key),\ncomposed with the same ruamel.yaml composer the loader uses, and must come back as a plain scalar\nwith exactly the same text, and, for values, typed as that same string by the shared\n:func:`~troupe.config.scalars.resolve_plain_scalar` (so ``0.2`` or ``true`` are never written plain\nas strings). Keys are compared as text only, as the loader treats keys textually.\n\nExisting styles are taken from the model (``MappingEntry.key_style``, ``ConfigScalar.style``) and\nnarrowed with :func:`quote_style_of`, never from span text. Strings starting with ``file:`` get no\nspecial treatment here (2.7).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Final, Literal, TypeAlias\n\nfrom ruamel.yaml import YAML\nfrom ruamel.yaml.error import YAMLError\nfrom ruamel.yaml.nodes import MappingNode, Node, ScalarNode, SequenceNode\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import WriteRefusedError\nfrom troupe.config.model import ScalarStyle\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.scalars import resolve_plain_scalar\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import NewScalar\n\n\nclass Context(Enum):\n    \"\"\"Where a scalar is written: as a value or a key, in a block or a flow collection.\"\"\"\n\n    BLOCK_VALUE = \"block-value\"\n    FLOW_VALUE = \"flow-value\"\n    BLOCK_KEY = \"bloc...[truncated 8686 chars]

The full suite passes (1245 passed, 0 skipped), and mypy, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean. Nothing is committed and `tasks.md` is untouched.\n\n- **(1) `<<` keys:** `_plain_possible` now says a key spelled `<<` can't be plain, because the loader refuses a plain `<<` key as a merge key. The loader's `_MERGE_KEY` constant is private, so I defined it once in `scalar_render.py` with a comment pointing at the loader rule. `choose_style` therefore falls back to single-quoted, giving `'<<'`.\n- **(2) Tests:** `<<` is in the representability table for both key contexts (not plain, single-quoted allowed) and for block values (plain is fine there). `test_render_key` has `<<` cases for both key contexts, with the sibling style set to plain and with no sibling style. Each asserts `'<<'` and that the file reloads through `load_config` with the same key text.\n- **(3) No skips:** the `file:` row is now filtered out of the reload test's parameters instead of being skipped at runtime.\n- **(4) RED:** I ran the new tests before changing the code; output below.\n\n## Status Report\n- STATUS: READY_FOR_REVIEW\n- TASK: 2.4\n- TASK_BRIEF: Decide whether plain and single quotes can represent a string (a syntactic check, then for plain a ruamel parse probe in the exact context: block or flow, value or key; for values the string must still read back as a string; a key `<<` is never plain because the loader refuses it as a merge key). Keep a representable existing or sibling style, otherwise fall back plain → single → double. Write non-strings plain with their VALUE spelling. In double quotes escape only `\`, `"` and control characters (named escapes including `\N`, otherwise upper-case `\xHH`); in single quotes write `'` as `''`. `quote_style_of` maps literal, folded and None to None. `file:` strings get no special treatment.\n- FILES_CHANGED: src/troupe/config/writeback/scalar_render.py, tests/writeback/test_scalar_render.py\n- REQUIREMENTS_CHECKED: 2.7, 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5, 6.6, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3 (7.4 is supported because `preferred=None` gives the minimal style)\n- DESIGN_CHECKED: Components and Interfaces › ScalarRender (Responsibilities & Constraints, Contracts: `Context`, `QuoteStyle`, `can_represent`, `choose_style`, `render_scalar`, `render_key`, `quote_style_of`); Testing Strategy › Unit Tests › ScalarRender; File Structure Plan\n- RED_PHASE_OUTPUT: Round 2, new `<<` tests run before the fix, `uv run pytest tests/writeback/test_scalar_render.py -q` → `8 failed, 284 passed`. Failing: `test_representability_table[<<-Context.BLOCK_KEY-False-True]`, `test_representability_table[<<-Context.FLOW_KEY-False-True]`, `test_every_representable_style_reads_back[<<-Context.BLOCK_KEY-False-True]`, `test_every_representable_style_reads_back[<<-Context.FLOW_KEY-False-True]`, `test_render_key[<<-Context.BLOCK_KEY-ScalarStyle.PLAIN-'<<']`, `test_render_key[<<-Context.BLOCK_KEY-None-'<<']`, `test_render_key[<<-Context.FLOW_KEY-ScalarStyle.PLAIN-'<<']`, `test_render_key[<<-Context.FLOW_KEY-None-'<<']`. tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"BlockScalar: literal rendering, chomping, header rewrite, folded paragraphs and wrapping.\n\nA multi-line string written in block context becomes a literal block (9.1): the header is ``|``\nfollowed by the chomping indicator the value's trailing line breaks require (strip ``-`` for none,\nclip for exactly one, keep ``+`` for more), and the content lines are the value's lines at a given\nindentation, empty lines written as bare line breaks (9.2). A string a literal block cannot hold\n(:func:`literal_fits` is false) is written double-quoted by the caller instead (9.7).\n\nFolded paragraphs are re-wrapped greedily by word with :func:`wrap_paragraph` (10.2, 10.5).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Final\n\n_FLAG_ENABLED: Final = False\n\n\nclass Chomping(Enum):\n    \"\"\"Block chomping indicator: strip (``-``), clip (nothing) or keep (``+``).\"\"\"\n\n    STRIP = \"-\"\n    CLIP = \"\"\n    KEEP = \"+\"\n\n\n_UNFIT: Final = re.compile(\"[\\x00-\\x08\\x0b-\\x1f\\x7f-\\x9f  \\ud800-\\udfff￾￿]\")\n\"\"\"Characters a literal block cannot hold (9.7): control characters other than TAB and LF\n(C0, DEL, C1 including U+0085), the Unicode line/paragraph separators, lone surrogates and the\nnon-characters U+FFFE/U+FFFF, none of which YAML accepts literally.\"\"\"\n\n_BREAK_POINT: Final = re.compile(r\"(?<=[^ ]) (?=[^ ])\")\n\"\"\"A single space with a non-space character on both sides: the only place a line may break (10.5).\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _trailing_breaks(value: str) -> int:\n    return len(value) - len(value.rstrip(\"\\n\"))\n\n\ndef required_chomping(value: str) -> Chomping:\n    \"\"\"The chomping a value's trailing line breaks require (9.1).\"\"\"\n    if not _FLAG_ENABLED:\n        raise NotImplementedError\n    trailing = _trailing_breaks(value)\n    if trailing == 0:\n        return Chomping.STRIP\n    return Chomping.CLIP if trailing == 1 else Chomping.KEEP\n\n\ndef chomping_fits(chomping: Chomping, value: str) -> bool:\n...[truncated 3810 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"CollectionRender: new block and flow collections and new entries as text lines.\n\nBlock style (8.1-8.4, 8.6, 9.1, 9.2): a mapping entry is ``{column}{key}: {inline}`` and a list item\n``{column}- {inline}``, each followed by a line break and the value's following lines. A nested\nmapping is written one indentation step right of its key, a nested list with its ``-`` indicators at\nthe file's dash offset from its key, and a collection that is a list item compactly: its first entry\nfollows ``- `` and its further entries are two columns right of the ``-``. A multi-line string is a\nliteral block whose content is one step right of its key (or ``-``), or double-quoted when a literal\nblock cannot hold it (9.7). An empty collection is ``{}``/``[]`` inline.\n\nFlow style (8.5, 8.6, 9.3): ``{k: v, k2: v2}`` and ``[a, b]``; multi-line strings are double-quoted.\n\nSibling styles (7.1-7.3) apply only to the first-level new key and value; every key and string\ninside a new collection is written in the minimal style (7.4).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Final\n\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.block_scalar import literal_fits, render_literal\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.scalar_render import Context, QuoteStyle, render_key, render_scalar\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import NewMapping, NewScalar, NewSequence, NewValue\n\n_COMPACT_INDENT: Final = 2\n\"\"\"Further entries of a list-item collection start this many columns right of its ``-`` (8.4).\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass RenderContext:\n    \"\"\"The file's layout conventions for new text, and the PATH of the set for errors.\"\"\"\n\n    step: int\n    \"\"\"Indentation step of nested block mappings and of literal block content (8.1, 9.2).\"\"\"\n    dash_offset: int\n    \"\"\"Offset of a block list's ``-`` from the key that holds it (8.3).\"\"\"\n    line_break: str\n    \"\"\"Line break written after every new ...[truncated 5252 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"PatchPlanner: slot changes, merges, new entries, deletions and kind changes.\n\nTurns a resolved :class:`~troupe.config.writeback.target.SetRequest` into the changed text of every\nfile the set must change, one :class:`FilePatch` per changed file, in the order the files appear in\nthe loaded document (root file first). Nothing is written here.\n\nA replaced value goes through :meth:`_Planner.change_slot`, which follows the design's \"slot change\ndecision\":\n\n* an unchanged value (typed plain equality) needs no edit;\n* a YAML include root that would change is refused (2.5); a text include gets its target file's\n  whole content replaced by the text-include content rule (2.2, 2.3), or is refused when VALUE is\n  not a string (2.4);\n* an existing literal or folded block changed to a string it can still hold is rewritten in place\n  (9.4, 9.5, 10.x);\n* an existing plain, quoted or empty scalar changed to a scalar is replaced in its slot in the\n  chosen quote style (6.1-6.3); a multi-line string becomes a literal block in a block collection\n  (9.1, 9.2) and a double-quoted scalar in a flow collection or where a literal block cannot hold\n  it (9.3, 9.7).\n\nEnd-of-line comments on the changed lines are moved back to their columns by the EditApplier\n(12.x). tool: Edit {"file_path": "/work/repo/src/troupe/config/writeback/planner.py", "new_string": "            _refuse(\n                path,\n                layout.file,\n                f\"this change cannot be written: {_kind(node)} cannot be replaced by \"\n                f\"{_kind(value)}\",\n            )\n\n    def _change_value(\n        self,\n        layout: FileLayout,\n        node: ConfigNode,\n        slot: ValueSlot,\n        value: NewValue,\n        path: ConfigPath,\n    ) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Plan an in-place change of a value that is not an include root; ``False`` if none fits.\n\n        Layout lookups raise ``ValueError`` for layouts outside the contract (``? key``); the\n        caller turns that into a refusal (14.9).\n        \"\"\"\n        if not (isinstance(node, ConfigScalar) and isinstance(value, NewScalar)):\n            return False\n        if node.style in _BLOCK_STYLES:\n            return isinstance(value.value, str) and self._rewrite_block(\n                layout, slot, node, value.value, path\n            )\n        if node.style in _QUOTED_OR_PLAIN:\n            self._replace_scalar(layout, slot, node, value, path)\n            return True\n        return False  # pragma: no cover - only text includes have no style\n", "old_string": "            _refuse(\n            path,\n            layout.file,\n            f\"this change cannot be written: {_kind(node)} cannot be replaced by {_kind(value)}\",\n        )\n", "replace_all": false}

tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > /tmp/probe.py <<'EOF'\nimport tempfile, pathlib\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.target import resolve_target\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import parse_value\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.planner import plan_patch\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.compare import node_to_plain, plain_equal\ncases=[(b\"? a\\n: 1\\n\",\"b\",\"2\"),(b\"m: {a: 1, b: }\\n\",\"m.c\",\"2\"),(b\"\\xef\\xbb\\xbfa: 1\\n\",\"b\",\"2\"),(b\"a: 1\\r\\nb: 2\\n\",\"c\",\"3\"),(b\"a: 1\\nb: 2\\r\\n\",\"c\",\"3\"),\n(b\"l:\\n  - a\\n  -\\n\",\"l.2\",\"b\"),(b\"m:\\n  a:\\n\",\"m.b\",\"1\"),(b\"\\xef\\xbb\\xbf\",\"a\",\"1\"),(b\"{}\\n\",\"a\",\"1\"),(b\"l: [a, b]\\n\",\"l.2\",\"\\\"x\\\\ny\\\"\"),(b\"a: {x: 1}  # c\\n\",\"a.y\",\"2\")]\nfor text,path,val in cases:\n    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); p=pathlib.Path(d)/\"troupe.yml\"; p.write_bytes(text)\n    try:\n        doc=load_config(p); cp=ConfigPath.parse(path); req=resolve_target(doc,cp,parse_value(val,cp))\n        pt=plan_patch(doc,req); new=pt[0].new_text\n        ok=plain_equal(node_to_plain(load_config(p,{doc.files[0].real_path:new}).root),req.intended,ordered=True)\n        print(repr(text),path,repr(new.encode()),ok)\n    except Exception as e: print(repr(text),path,type(e).__name__,e)\nEOF\nuv run python /tmp/probe.py", "description": "Probe edge cases"}

tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > /tmp/probe33.py <<'EOF'\nimport sys, tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.target import resolve_target\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.planner import plan_patch\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import parse_value\ncases = [\n (\"a:\\n  b: 1\\n  # trailing\\n# top comment\\nc: 2\\n\",\"a.x\",\"5\"),\n (\"items:\\n  - a\\n  - b\\n\\nother: 1\\n\",\"items.2\",\"c\"),\n (\"m: {a: 1}  # c\\n\",\"m.b\",\"2\"),\n ('k: \"x\"\\n',\"n\",\"y\"),\n (\"a: {}\\n\",\"a.b.c\",\"1\"),\n (\"\",\"a\",\"1\"),\n (\"a: 1\",\"b\",\"2\"),\n (\"a:\\n  b: 1\\n    # deeper\\n  # same\\n # less\\nc: 1\\n\",\"a.x\",\"2\"),\n (\"l: [a, b,]\\n\",\"l.2\",\"c\"),\n (\"l: []\\n\",\"l.0\",\"c\"),\n (\"a: x\\n\",\"b\",\"\\\"one\\\\ntwo\\\\n\\\"\"),\n (\"m: {a: 1}\\n\",\"m.b\",\"\\\"one\\\\ntwo\\\\n\\\"\"),\n (\"a:\\n  b: 1\\n\",\"a.c\",\"{x: 1, y: [1, 2]}\"),\n (\"a:\\n    b: 1\\nz: 1\\n\",\"a.c.d\",\"1\"),\n (\"l:\\n- a\\n- b\\n\",\"l.2\",\"{x: 1}\"),\n (\"l:\\n  - a\\n\",\"l.5\",\"c\"),\n (\"'k': 'x'\\n\",\"n\",\"y\"),\n (\"a: x\\n\",\"b\",\"\\\"one\\\\ntwo\\\"\"),\n (\"a: 1 # c\\nb:\\n  c: 1 # x\",\"b.d\",\"\\\"l1\\\\nl2\\\\n\\\"\"),\n (\"m: {a: 1,\\n  b: 2}\\n\",\"m.c\",\"3\"),\n (\"a: 1\\r\\nb: 2\\r\\n\",\"c\",\"3\"),\n]\nfor text, path, val in cases:\n    d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())\n    (d/\"troupe.yml\").write_text(text)\n    try:\n        doc = load_config(d/\"troupe.yml\")\n        cp = ConfigPath.parse(path)\n        req = resolve_target(doc, cp, parse_value(val, cp))\n        ps = plan_patch(doc, req)\n        print(repr(text), path, val, \"->\", [repr(p.new_text) for p in ps])\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(repr(text), path, val, \"EXC\", type(e).__name__, e)\nEOF\nuv run python /tmp/probe33.py"}

tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > /tmp/probe33b.py <<'EOF'\nimport tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.target import resolve_target\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.planner import plan_patch\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import parse_value\ncases = [\n (\"a:\\n  b: 1\\n\\n  # c\\n\\nz: 1\\n\",\"a.x\",\"2\",{}),\n (\"# only comment\\n\",\"a\",\"1\",{}),\n (\"# only comment\",\"a\",\"1\",{}),\n (\"a: x\\n\",\"b\",\"'\\\"true\\\"'\",{}),\n (\"a: x\\n\",\"b\",\"'\\\"a: b\\\"'\",{}),\n (\"a: x\\n\",\"\\\"1\\\"\",\"1\",{}),\n (\"a: x\\n\",\"a.b\",\"1\",{}),\n (\"a: [1]\\n\",\"a.1.x\",\"1\",{}),\n (\"agents:\\n  coder: file:coder.yaml\\n\",\"agents.coder.temp\",\"1\",{\"coder.yaml\":\"model: y\\n\"}),\n (\"agents:\\n  coder: file:coder.yaml\\n\",\"agents.coder.p.q\",\"1\",{\"coder.yaml\":\"model: y\"}),\n (\"l:\\n  - a\\n\",\"l.1\",\"\\\"x\\\\ny\\\\n\\\"\",{}),\n (\"a:\\n  - 1\\n  # c\\n# d\\nb: 2\\n\",\"a.1\",\"{p: 1, q: 2}\",{}),\n (\"a: x\\n\",\"b\",\"\\\"\\\"\",{}),\n (\"a:\\n  b: |\\n    t\\n\\n\\nz: 1\\n\",\"a.c\",\"1\",{}),\n (\"m: {a: }\\n\",\"m.b\",\"2\",{}),\n (\"m:\\n  a:\\n\",\"m.b\",\"2\",{}),\n]\nfor text, path, val, files in cases:\n    d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())\n    (d/\"troupe.yml\").write_text(text)\n    for n,t in files.items(): (d/n).write_text(t)\n    try:\n        doc = load_config(d/\"troupe.yml\")\n        cp = ConfigPath.parse(path)\n        req = resolve_target(doc, cp, parse_value(val, cp))\n        ps = plan_patch(doc, req)\n        print(repr(text), path, val, \"->\", [(p.file.path.name, p.new_text) for p in ps])\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(repr(text), path, val, \"EXC\", type(e).__name__, e)\nEOF\nuv run python /tmp/probe33b.py"}

tool: Bash {"command": "cd /work/repo; cat > /tmp/probe.py <<'EOF'\nimport tempfile, pathlib\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.compare import node_to_plain, plain_equal\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.planner import plan_patch\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.target import resolve_target\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import parse_value\ncases=[(\"l:\\n  -   # c\\n    a: 1\\n\",\"l.0\",\"5\"),(\"l:\\n  - - a\\n    - b\\nn: 1\\n\",\"l.0\",\"x\"),\n(\"a:\\n  foo\\nb: 1\\n\",\"a\",\"{x: 1}\"),(\"a: |+\\n  t\\n\\n\",\"a\",\"5\"),(\"a: |+\\n  t\\n\",\"a\",\"[1]\"),\n(\"a:\\n  x: 1\\n\",\"a\",\"[]\"),(\"l:\\n- a: 1  # c\\n  b: 2\\n\",\"l.0\",\"[p, q]\"),(\"a: {x: 1}\\n\",\"a\",\"[]\"),\n(\"a:\\n- 1\\nb: x\\n\",\"b\",\"[p]\"),(\"a: x\\n\",\"a\",'\"one\\\\n\"'),(\"a:\\n  b:\\n    c: 1\\n  d: 2\\n\",\"a.b\",\"q\")]\nfor text,path,val in cases:\n    d=pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); (d/\"troupe.yml\").write_text(text)\n    doc=load_config(d/\"troupe.yml\"); p=ConfigPath.parse(path)\n    req=resolve_target(doc,p,parse_value(val,p))\n    try:\n        pt=plan_patch(doc,req)\n        new=pt[0].new_text\n        r=load_config(d/\"troupe.yml\",{doc.root_file.real_path:new})\n        print(repr(text),path,val,'->',repr(new), plain_equal(node_to_plain(r.root),req.intended,ordered=True))\n    except Exception as e: print(repr(text),path,val,'ERR',type(e).__name__,e)\nEOF\nuv run python /tmp/probe.py"}

Every file of the loaded document is\noverridden with its loaded text and every patched file with its new text; targets of includes\nwritten by this set are not overridden and are read (never written) from disk by the loader,\nexactly as a later ``show`` would read them. Any load error (including a missing, unreadable or\nunloadable target of a new include and an include cycle) and any difference from the intended\nconfiguration (including key order and include directives) is a :class:`WriteRefusedError`\n(exit 3) naming the first patched file and PATH (14.2, 14.8).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import ConfigLoadError, WriteRefusedError\nfrom troupe.config.loader import load_config\nfrom troupe.config.model import ConfigDocument\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.compare import node_to_plain, plain_equal\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.planner import FilePatch\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.target import SetRequest\n\n\ndef verify_patch(\n    config_file: Path,\n    document: ConfigDocument,\n    patches: Sequence[FilePatch],\n    request: SetRequest,\n) -> ConfigDocument:\n    \"\"\"Re-load ``config_file`` with all ``patches`` applied in memory and return the result.\n\n    Raises :class:`WriteRefusedError` naming the first patched file and PATH when the patched\n    configuration cannot be loaded (the problem carries the loader's message, which names the\n    failing file and, for includes, the include target) or when it differs from\n    ``request.intended`` (ordered comparison; further patched files are listed in the problem).\n    \"\"\"\n    if not patches:  # pragma: no cover - plan_patch never returns an empty plan\n        raise ValueError(\"v...[truncated 972 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"Unit tests of the AtomicWriter (task 4.3): ``troupe.config.writeback.atomic``.\n\nEvery test writes real files in a temporary directory. Failures are injected at the OS boundary\n(``os.replace``, ``os.write``, ``os.fsync``, an unwritable directory) to prove that the target keeps\nits previous bytes and that no temporary file is left behind (product-owner decision E).\n\nTraceability: every test names the requirement IDs it proves at the start of its docstring.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport re\nimport stat\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom set_support import assert_file_bytes, snapshot_tree\nfrom troupe.config.errors import ExitCode, WriteRefusedError\nfrom troupe.config.model import LineEnding, SourceFile\nfrom troupe.config.writeback import atomic\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.atomic import restore_file, write_atomically\n\nTEMP_NAME = re.compile(r\"^\\.troupe\\.yml\\.troupe-tmp-[0-9a-f]{16}$\")\n\n\ndef _source(path: Path, text: str) -> SourceFile:\n    \"\"\"Return the SourceFile the loader would produce for ``path`` holding ``text``.\"\"\"\n    return SourceFile(path=path, real_path=path.resolve(), text=text, line_ending=LineEnding.LF)\n\n\ndef _make(directory: Path, name: str, data: bytes, mode: int = 0o644) -> Path:\n    file = directory / name\n    file.write_bytes(data)\n    file.chmod(mode)\n    return file\n\n\ndef _listing(directory: Path) -> list[str]:\n    return sorted(os.listdir(directory))\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef unwritable_dir_supported(tmp_path: Path) -> Iterator[None]:\n    probe = tmp_path / \"probe\"\n    probe.mkdir()\n    probe.chmod(0o555)\n    try:\n        writable = os.access(probe, os.W_OK)\n    finally:\n        probe.chmod(0o755)\n        probe.rmdir()\n    if writable:\n        pytest.skip(\"directory permissions are not enforced for this user (root?)\")\n    yield\n\n\ndef test_writes_new_bytes_and_keeps_listing(tmp_path: Path)...[truncated 9017 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"AtomicWriter: the only writer of user files (atomic replace next to the target, restore).\n\nA write goes to ``SourceFile.real_path`` (a symbolic link is written through and stays a link): the\nUTF-8 bytes of the text (a BOM in the text is kept; no newline translation) are written to an\nexclusively created hidden temporary file ``.<name>.troupe-tmp-<16 hex>`` in the target's directory\nwith the target's permission bits, flushed and synced, then renamed over the target. On any failure\nthe temporary file is removed and a :class:`WriteRefusedError` naming the file is raised; the\ncaller adds PATH. No extra file remains after any handled outcome (product-owner decision E).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport contextlib\nimport os\nimport secrets\nimport stat\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import WriteRefusedError\nfrom troupe.config.model import SourceFile\n\n_TEMP_INFIX = \".troupe-tmp-\"\n_CREATE_FLAGS = os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY | getattr(os, \"O_CLOEXEC\", 0)\n_MAX_NAME_ATTEMPTS = 16\n\n_ATOMIC_WRITES_ENABLED = False\n\n\ndef write_atomically(file: SourceFile, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Replace the content of ``file.real_path`` with ``text`` encoded as UTF-8, atomically.\n\n    Raises :class:`WriteRefusedError` (``file=file.path``) when the file cannot be written; the\n    target then keeps its previous content and no temporary file remains.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not _ATOMIC_WRITES_ENABLED:\n        return\n    try:\n        data = text.encode(\"utf-8\")\n    except UnicodeEncodeError as error:\n        raise WriteRefusedError(\n            f\"cannot write file: text is not valid UTF-8 ({error.reason})\", file=file.path\n        ) from error\n    target = file.real_path\n    try:\n        mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(target).st_mode)\n        temp, descriptor = _create_temp(target, mode)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise WriteRefusedError(f\"cannot write file: {_reason(error)}\", file=file.path) from error\n    repla...[truncated 1693 chars]

tool: Write {"content": "\"\"\"SetCommand: the ``set_value`` use case (no-op, plan, verify, write all, roll back, record).\n\nEverything up to the first write is pure: the target is resolved on ``theatre.document`` (the files\nas on disk, product-owner decision A), a no-op returns before planning (14.6), every patch is\nplanned and verified together (13.6) and the history changes are derived, so a refusal changes no\nfile (14.7). Then every patch is written atomically in order; when a write fails, the files already\nwritten are restored in reverse order and the failure is re-raised with PATH (14.5, 16.2). The\nchanges are recorded in one batch only after every write succeeded; when recording fails, every\nwritten file is restored and the store error is re-raised (15.6). A failing restore never stops the\nremaining restores; the original error keeps its exit code and names each unrestored file (14.10).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom troupe.config.errors import TroupeError, WriteRefusedError\nfrom troupe.config.history import LeafChange\nfrom troupe.config.model import SourceFile\nfrom troupe.config.paths import ConfigPath\nfrom troupe.config.theatre import Theatre\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.atomic import restore_file, write_atomically\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.compare import plain_equal\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.leaf_diff import diff_leaves\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.planner import FilePatch, plan_patch\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.target import resolve_target\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.value import NewValue\nfrom troupe.config.writeback.verify import verify_patch\n\n_ENABLED = False\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass SetOutcome:\n    \"\"\"The result of a set: the written files (in write order) and the recorded changes.\"\"\"\n\n    written: tuple[Path, ...]  # empty for a no-op\n    changes: tuple[LeafChange, ...]\n\n\ndef set_value(theatre: Theatre, path: ConfigPath, value...[truncated 3225 chars]

PATH and VALUE are the\nexact argv strings, written as Python literals; the fixture and the expected text are the exact\nbytes of ``.troupe/troupe.yml`` (UTF-8). Each case asserts exit 0, empty stdout, empty stderr,\nthe exact bytes of troupe.yml and that no other file was added, removed or changed.\n\nTraceability: every test names the requirement IDs it proves at the start of its docstring.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom set_support import TreeSnapshot, assert_file_bytes, run_set, snapshot_tree\nfrom support import CliResult, MakeTheatre\n\nROOT = \".troupe/troupe.yml\"\n\n\ndef _assert_success(result: CliResult) -> None:\n    assert (result.exit_code, result.stdout, result.stderr) == (0, b\"\", \"\"), result.stderr\n\n\ndef _assert_only_root_changed(theatre: Path, before: TreeSnapshot, expected: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Assert troupe.yml holds exactly ``expected`` and every other file is unchanged.\"\"\"\n    assert_file_bytes(theatre / ROOT, expected)\n    after = snapshot_tree(theatre)\n    assert set(after) == set(before)\n    assert {k: v for k, v in after.items() if k != ROOT} == {\n        k: v for k, v in before.items() if k != ROOT\n    }\n\n\ndef _set_and_check(\n    make_theatre: MakeTheatre, fixture: str, path: str, value: str, expected: str\n) -> None:\n    theatre = make_theatre(fixture)\n    before = snapshot_tree(theatre)\n    result = run_set(theatre, path, value)\n    _assert_success(result)\n    _assert_only_root_changed(theatre, before, expected)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"fixture\", \"path\", \"value\", \"expected\"),\n    [\n        pytest.param(\"a: 1    # c\\nb: 2\\n\", \"a\", \"100\", \"a: 100  # c\\nb: 2\\n\", id=\"longer\"),\n        pytest.param(\"a: 1000 # c\\n\", \"a\", \"1\", \"a: 1    # c\\n\", id=\"shorter\"),\n    ],\...[truncated 1892 chars]

PATH and VALUE are the exact argv strings, written as Python literals; fixtures are\nthe exact bytes of the files.\n\nEach history line is parsed with strict JSON (no NaN/Infinity constants) and asserted for ``seq``,\n``op``, ``path``, ``old`` and ``new``, with the JSON type of every value checked too (``1``,\n``1.0`` and ``\"1\"`` are different values).\n\nTraceability: every test names the requirement IDs it proves at the start of its docstring.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport pytest\nfrom eventsourcing.sqlite import SQLiteCursor\n\nfrom set_support import (\n    assert_file_bytes,\n    run_config,\n    run_config_in_process,\n    run_set,\n    set_args,\n)\nfrom support import CliResult, MakeTheatre\nfrom troupe.config.constants import HISTORY_STORE_NAME\n\nROOT = \".troupe/troupe.yml\"\n\nEvent = tuple[int, str, str, object, object]\n\"\"\"One history line as ``(seq, op, path, old, new)``.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _reject_constant(name: str) -> object:\n    raise ValueError(f\"non-strict JSON constant {name}\")\n\n\ndef _typed(value: object) -> object:\n    \"\"\"``value`` paired with its exact JSON type, so ``1``, ``1.0``, ``True`` and ``\"1\"`` differ.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, list):\n        return (\"list\", [_typed(item) for item in value])\n    if isinstance(value, dict):\n        return (\"dict\", {key: _typed(item) for key, item in value.items()})\n    return (type(value).__name__, value)\n\n\ndef _events(theatre: Path, path: str | None = None) -> list[Event]:\n    \"\"\"Every ``troupe config history [PATH]`...[truncated 10216 chars]
